description: a wildfire sensor sends a smoke alert to the dispatch center, which checks it against satellite images. if the satellite confirms a fire dispatch pages the duty ranger, otherwise it logs a false alarm and keeps watching the sensor. the ranger drives out and estimates the spread, and unless the wind is above forty kilometres an hour the ranger sends a ground crew. when the wind is too strong the ranger calls the regional command, which orders an evacuation through the county sheriff. the sheriff texts every resident in the zone, and residents who don't reply within ten minutes get a door knock from a deputy. once the crew contains the fire they report back to dispatch, which closes the incident.

errors.detail: The wind condition is split into two decision boxes. 'Wind above 40 km/h?' has only a 'no' edge to Ground Crew, and 'Wind too strong?' has only a 'yes' edge to Regional Command, so neither has both outcomes and the second box is redundant.

The edge Door Knock -> Deputy 'handled by' runs backwards. The deputy performs the door knock, so it should be Deputy -> Door Knock, and the residents who get no door knock are never shown to receive it.
The ten-minute reply window is missing from the 'Resident silent?' decision.

description: the transplant coordinator gets a donor kidney and runs it through the matching system. the matching system ranks waiting patients by blood type and tissue match and sends the top patient to the surgeon. if the surgeon accepts the organ the hospital calls the patient in, otherwise the matching system offers it to the next patient on the list. when the patient arrives the lab cross-matches their blood again and only if the cross-match is negative does the surgery go ahead, else the kidney goes back to the matching system. after surgery the recovery ward monitors the patient and pages the surgeon if creatinine rises.

errors.detail: A negative cross-match sends the flow back to the Surgeon, who is the box that feeds the 'Surgeon accepts?' decision. With no separate Surgery step, the process appears to re-ask acceptance instead of proceeding to surgery.

There is no Surgery step between the negative cross-match and the Recovery Ward. The text says monitoring happens after surgery, but the diagram goes Surgeon to Recovery Ward and labels that edge 'pages'.
The edge Surgeon -> Recovery Ward labeled 'pages' reverses the text. The Recovery Ward pages the surgeon, and that is already covered by the Creatinine rises? -> Surgeon edge.
'Next Patient' is used in an edge but is not in the boxes list, and it leads nowhere. The offer to the next patient never continues to the surgeon or the hospital call-in.

description: telemetry from the satellite comes down through a ground station, and there is a decoder in front of the mission database. the decoder checks every frame's checksum and drops it if the checksum fails, otherwise it writes the frame to the mission database. an anomaly detector reads the database every minute and if a reading is out of range it alerts the flight controller. the flight controller decides whether it's a real fault; if it is they upload a safe-mode command back to the satellite through the ground station, if it isn't they mark the alert as noise. the database is replicated and uses round robin.

errors.detail: The 'Checksum failed?' decision has no 'no' outcome, so frames that pass the checksum are never written to the mission database.
The safe-mode command goes to the Ground Station but no edge continues from the Ground Station to the Satellite, so the upload back to the satellite is absent.
The Satellite box has no edge to Telemetry or the Ground Station, so the origin of the telemetry is not connected.
The 'Frame Log' box is not in the text; a frame that fails the checksum is simply dropped, not logged.

description: a customer files a car insurance claim in the app, and the app sends it to the claims service. the claims service runs a fraud model on it. claims the model scores as high risk go to the special investigations unit, the rest go to an adjuster. the adjuster asks the customer for photos and if the photos are missing the adjuster chases the customer again. when the damage is under two thousand dollars the adjuster approves payment straight away, otherwise a senior adjuster has to sign off first. finance pays the approved claims and emails the customer a receipt. investigators who find fraud refer the claim to the police.

errors.detail: Senior Adjuster has no outgoing edge, so the sign-off never leads to Payment Approved and the flow dead-ends.
Special Investigations is not connected to Investigators, so claims sent to the unit never reach the investigators and the police-referral path is disconnected.
Investigators refer to the police only if they find fraud, but there is no 'Fraud found?' decision box and the referral is unconditional.
The 'Photos missing?' yes edge returns to Adjuster rather than to Customer, though the adjuster chases the customer again.
'Photos missing?' has no 'no' outcome, and the Adjuster goes straight to the damage check without waiting for photos, so the photos-received path is absent. The box is also not in the boxes list.

description: the stage manager calls the cue on headset and the lighting operator presses go on the console. the console sends the cue over the network to the dimmer racks, and there is a network switch in front of the dimmer racks. if a dimmer rack doesn't acknowledge the cue the console retries it twice, and if it still fails the operator switches to the backup console. the follow spot operators also listen to the stage manager and pick up the lead actor when the stage manager says so. at the end of the act the stage manager tells the house manager, who opens the bar.

errors.detail: The Lighting Operator is not connected to the Stage Manager or the headset cue, so nothing shows the cue triggering the operator pressing go.
The 'Dimmer failed?' decision is checked from Dimmer Racks, but the Console is the box that waits for the acknowledgement and decides to retry.

The 'no' outcome (cue acknowledged) leads to Backup Console, and 'yes' leads to a dead-end 'Retry Console' box. The backup console should only be used after the retries still fail, and a successful acknowledgement should not trigger anything.
The console retrying the cue twice is missing: no edge sends the retry back to the Dimmer Racks, and there is no second 'still fails?' check before the operator switches to the Backup Console.
Follow Spot Operators never pick up the Lead Actor. The 'Stage Manager says so?' decision box is orphaned and never connects the operators to the actor.
The edge Stage Manager -> Lead Actor 'says so' is not in the text. The Stage Manager gives the cue to the follow spot operators, not to the actor.

description: a beekeeper inspects each hive every week and records it in the hive log. if the beekeeper sees queen cells they split the colony into a new hive, otherwise they check the honey supers. supers that are more than eighty percent capped go to the extraction room, which spins them and sends the honey to the bottling line. the bottling line labels the jars only when the moisture reading is under eighteen percent; wetter honey goes back to the extraction room to dry. a distributor collects the labelled jars on fridays.

errors.detail: The diagram adds a separate 'Spinning Room' box, but the text says the extraction room itself spins the supers and sends the honey on. The flow is unchanged, so this is a harmless extra step.

description: the passenger books a ferry ticket on the website, which asks the booking engine for a space on the sailing. the booking engine checks vehicle deck capacity and if the deck is full it puts the passenger on the waitlist, otherwise it holds a space and sends the passenger to payment. if the payment fails the booking engine releases the space. the waitlist service watches for cancellations and offers freed spaces to waitlisted passengers by sms. on the day the port gate scans the ticket and lets the car board unless the ticket is for a different sailing, in which case the gate sends the driver to the ticket office.

errors.detail: The payment failure condition has no decision box: 'fails?' is put in an edge label from Payment back to Booking Engine, so the 'Booking Engine releases Space' edge is unconditional and the failure/success branches are not modelled.
The edge Booking Engine -> Sailing labeled 'routes to' is not described; the sailing is only the thing the space is requested on, and this edge misuses the 'routes to' meaning.
The Waitlist Service offers spaces to 'Waitlisted Passenger', which is not in the boxes list, so the edge is invalid and the offer is not tied to the Passenger or Waitlist boxes.
The Waitlist -> Waitlist Service edge 'watches for cancellations' runs in the wrong direction and is not linked to cancelled or freed Space, so the freed-space source is not shown.

description: a clinic refers a patient to the clinical trial, and the research nurse screens them against the eligibility criteria. ineligible patients are referred back to the clinic. eligible patients sign a consent form, and the randomisation system assigns them to the drug arm or the placebo arm. the pharmacy dispenses the blinded kit for whichever arm they're in. every two weeks the nurse records side effects and if a side effect is serious the nurse reports it to the safety board within a day. the safety board can unblind the patient, and if the drug caused it the board stops the patient's treatment.

errors.detail: The 'no' (eligible) outcome of 'Ineligible?' is missing. Eligible patients never go on to sign the Consent Form, so Consent Form has no incoming edge and the main flow is broken.
Clinical Trial is not connected to the Research Nurse, so the referral never leads to screening and the nurse step is disconnected from the start of the process.
'Ineligible?' is checked from the Eligibility Criteria box, but the research nurse makes the screening decision.
The 'yes' outcome of 'Drug caused?' goes to Unblinded Patient. The text says the board stops the patient's treatment, and there is no stop-treatment box or edge.
The edge 'Unblinded Patient receives Drug Arm' is invented. Unblinding could reveal either arm, and the text says nothing of the kind.
The decision box 'Drug caused?' is used in edges but is not in the boxes list. The 'no' outcome of 'Drug caused?' and the 'no' outcome of 'Serious?' are also missing.
The recurring two-weekly recording of side effects is not drawn as a loop. Nothing returns to the nurse's recording step after the check.
Pharmacy dispensing is not connected to the consent or randomisation flow. The kit is shown only as linked to the arms, and no recipient is shown.

description: trucks tip mixed recycling onto the intake belt, which carries it past a magnet that pulls out steel cans into the steel bay. the remaining material goes to an optical sorter which blows plastic bottles onto the plastics belt and lets paper fall through to the paper baler. a quality inspector watches the plastics belt and throws any paper back onto the intake belt. if the paper baler jams the line supervisor stops the intake belt until a mechanic clears it. full bales go to the loading dock where a buyer's truck collects them.

errors.detail: The remaining material after the magnet should go from the Magnet to the Optical Sorter, but the diagram routes it from the Steel Bay, so the steel bay wrongly feeds the sorter.
Full bales go from the Paper Baler to the Loading Dock regardless of jams. The diagram only reaches the Loading Dock through the 'no jam' branch, so bales are never delivered after a jam is cleared.
The mechanic clears the jam and the supervisor's stop lasts only until then, but the Mechanic has no outgoing edge and nothing restarts the intake belt or baler.

description: a player clicks find match and the client sends the request to the matchmaker. the matchmaker looks for players within one hundred rating points, and if it can't find nine others within thirty seconds it widens the range and searches again. once ten players are found the matchmaker asks the server allocator for a game server, and if no server is free in the player's region the allocator falls back to the nearest region. the game server loads the map and the clients connect to it. there's an anti-cheat service in front of the game server that kicks any client that fails its check. when the match ends the game server sends results to the rating service, which updates every player's rating.

errors.detail: The widening is triggered by 'Within 100 points?' being no, but the text widens only when nine others aren't found within thirty seconds. 'Within 30 seconds?' then only has a yes edge looping back to the search.

The success path of the search is missing. 'Ten players found?' is an orphan box, 'Within 100 points?' has no yes outcome, 'Within 30 seconds?' has no no outcome, and the matchmaker goes straight to the allocator.

The allocator's yes path (a server is free in the player's region) is missing. The nearest-region fallback 'Region' dead-ends and nothing leads from the allocator or the region to the game server, so the game server is never allocated.
'Game server -> Client: loads map' is wrong. The game server loads the map itself, and the clients connect to the game server, not the other way around.

The anti-cheat is in front of the game server, so it should take over the edges into the game server (client and allocator connections go to anti-cheat, which routes to the game server). The diagram has 'Anti-cheat -> Game server' labeled 'kicks failing client' instead of a kick edge from anti-cheat back to the client.
There is no 'Check failed?' decision for the anti-cheat. The yes outcome (kick the client) and the no outcome (the client proceeds to the game server) are both missing.

description: the avalanche forecaster reads the overnight snow sensors every morning and rates the danger from one to five. when the rating is three or below the ski patrol opens the slopes as normal, the rest of the time the forecaster asks the patrol leader for a control mission. the patrol leader checks the weather and only if visibility is good does the helicopter fly the explosives team up, otherwise the mission waits an hour and the patrol leader checks again. after the blasts the team inspects each slope, and slopes that slid cleanly reopen while the others stay closed. the patrol leader reports every closure back to the forecaster.

errors.detail: On the 'yes' path (rating three or below), Ski Patrol never opens the slopes. The path dead-ends at Ski Patrol with no edge to the slopes.

Helicopter has no edge to Explosives Team, so the helicopter never flies the team up. Explosives Team has no incoming edge, and the blasts step is missing, so the mission path never reaches the inspection.

The 'no' outcome of 'Slid cleanly?' loops back to Slopes, creating a cycle. The text says those slopes stay closed, which needs a closed-slopes outcome that feeds the patrol leader's closure report to the forecaster.

description: a donor gives blood at the mobile clinic and the courier takes the bag to the blood bank. the lab tests every bag for infections and discards any bag that tests positive, the clean ones get separated into plasma and red cells. red cells go to the cold store and plasma goes to the freezer. when a hospital orders blood the dispatcher picks the oldest matching unit from the cold store, and on a miss it falls back to the regional blood bank. the dispatcher sends the unit by courier and the hospital confirms receipt.

errors.detail: Nothing connects the Blood Bank to the Lab, so the bags the courier delivers never reach testing.
A positive test ('yes') goes to Red Cells instead of being discarded, and the clean path ('no') goes only to Plasma.
There is no discard box for bags that test positive.
The separation of clean bags into plasma and red cells is missing, so Red Cells and Plasma are not both reached from the clean outcome.
The 'Unit found?' decision is checked by the Cold Store, but the text has the dispatcher pick the unit and fall back on a miss.
The Oldest Unit and Regional Blood Bank outcomes dead-end. Neither leads to the Dispatcher sending the unit, so the fallback supply never reaches the hospital.
The Courier has no edge to the Hospital for delivery. The Hospital's 'confirms receipt' edge goes to the Courier, but the text has the hospital confirming receipt of the delivered unit.

description: each morning the vineyard manager samples grapes from every block and measures the sugar. blocks above twenty four brix get picked that day, the others are sampled again tomorrow. the pickers load the grapes into bins and a tractor hauls the bins to the crush pad. at the crush pad the sorting table removes leaves and rotten bunches, and the destemmer sends the clean fruit to the fermentation tanks. the winemaker tastes each tank daily and if fermentation stalls she adds yeast, else she leaves it until it's dry.

errors.detail: "Sample Tomorrow" is a dead end; the text says blocks at or below 24 brix are sampled again tomorrow, so it should loop back to the vineyard manager's sampling of the blocks.

"Add Yeast" dead-ends, although the winemaker tastes each tank daily and so should check the tank again after adding yeast. The "no" path to "Dry Wine" likewise has no return to daily tasting while the wine is left to dry.

description: the dentist scans the patient's tooth and uploads the scan to the dental lab portal. the portal queues it for a designer, who models the crown and sends the design back to the dentist for approval. if the dentist asks for changes the designer reworks it, otherwise the design goes to the milling machine. the milling machine cuts the crown from a zirconia block and the furnace sinters it. a technician checks the fit on a printed model and anything that doesn't fit goes back to the milling machine, the rest are shipped to the dentist.

errors.detail: The 'Changes needed?' decision is checked by the Designer, but the text says the dentist decides whether changes are needed, so the edge into it should come from the Dentist.
The 'yes' branch ends at 'Reworked Model' with no outgoing edge, so the designer's rework never loops back to the designer or on to dentist approval.
There is no edge from the Furnace to the Technician. The sintered crown never reaches the fit check, so the Technician branch is disconnected from the main flow.

description: a broadcaster uploads a film to the subtitling platform, which sends the audio to the speech recogniser. the recogniser produces a draft transcript and a translator corrects it and translates it. a reviewer watches the film with the subtitles and returns any scene with timing errors to the translator. once the reviewer signs off the platform burns the subtitles into a preview, and only when the broadcaster approves the preview does the platform deliver the final files. rejected previews go back to the reviewer.

errors.detail: The draft transcript goes from the Speech Recogniser straight to the Reviewer. The text sends it to the Translator, who corrects and translates it before the Reviewer sees anything.
The Translator has no outgoing edge, so the flow dead-ends there. The text has the Reviewer watch the film with the translated subtitles, so the Translator should hand off to the Reviewer.

The send-back of rejected previews is drawn as an unconditional Preview → Reviewer edge. The decision box 'Broadcaster approves?' has no 'no' edge, so the rejection path is not tied to the broadcaster's decision.
There is no decision box for 'timing errors?' after the Reviewer. The error send-back and the sign-off are two unconditional edges, and the sign-off is not tied to the no-errors case.
The platform's burning of subtitles into the preview is not shown as a step. The Reviewer connects directly to Preview, skipping the Subtitling Platform.

description: a reader emails the newspaper about a mistake and the email lands in the corrections inbox. the standards editor reads it and asks the reporter who wrote the story whether it's wrong. if the reporter agrees the standards editor writes a correction, if not the editor checks the source documents herself. corrections for print stories go to the night desk for tomorrow's paper, the rest are added to the web article straight away. the standards editor replies to the reader either way.

errors.detail: There is no edge from Corrections Inbox to Standards Editor, so the editor never reads the emailed complaint and the inbox dead-ends.
The extra 'Wrong?' decision, with Reporter feeding it and its 'yes' edge looping back to Standards Editor, is not in the text. It duplicates the reporter-agrees decision and has no 'no' branch.
'Reporter agrees?' is checked by Standards Editor, but the reporter is the one who answers whether the story is wrong.
The 'no' outcome of 'Reporter agrees?' loops back to Standards Editor. The text says the editor checks the source documents herself, and that step is absent.
There is no 'Print story?' decision. Every correction goes to the Night Desk, and the 'rest' path straight to the Web Article is missing.
The edge from Night Desk to Web Article is invented. Print corrections go to the night desk, and the other corrections go directly to the web article.
The reply edge goes from Standards Editor to Reporter. The text says the editor replies to the Reader, whichever way the check turns out.

description: customers upload models to the print farm website and the slicer turns each model into print instructions. the scheduler sends jobs to the printers, there are twelve printers and the scheduler uses least connections. a camera watches every print and if it spots spaghetti it cancels the job and the scheduler requeues it. finished prints go to the post processing bench where a worker removes supports. prints that need painting go to the paint booth first, the others go straight to packing, and the courier collects from packing at five.

errors.detail: The website never feeds the slicer, and the print instructions never go to the scheduler. The upload-to-slicer-to-scheduler flow is broken, and the scheduler has no input except the requeue.
The camera has no edge from the printers, so nothing shows it watching the prints. The spaghetti check is disconnected from the printing.
The printer goes straight to the Paint Booth, but finished prints go to the post-processing bench, and only those that need painting go on to the paint booth.
There is no 'Needs painting?' decision after post-processing. The 'no' path straight to Packing is missing, and the bench and worker dead-end.
The edge from Packing to Print Instructions ('handles') is not in the text and sends the flow backwards.

The printers appear as two separate boxes, 'Printer (least connections)' and 'Printers (twelve)', joined by a made-up 'routes to' edge. There should be one replicated printer box, and the downstream edges leave from the wrong one.

description: the pilot requests pushback from ground control, which checks the departure queue. if the queue is longer than ten aircraft ground control holds the pilot at the gate, otherwise it clears the pushback. the pilot taxis to the runway holding point and switches to the tower. the tower clears the aircraft for takeoff unless another aircraft is on final approach, in which case the pilot waits and asks again. after takeoff the tower hands the aircraft to departure control.

errors.detail: The Pushback box dead-ends. The pilot's taxi to the runway holding point is drawn from Pilot rather than following the pushback clearance, so taxiing looks independent of the queue decision.
The hand-off to Departure Control starts at Takeoff Clearance, but the text says the tower hands the aircraft over after takeoff. The takeoff itself is not shown.

description: each turbine streams vibration data to the monitoring centre, where a wear model scores it. turbines with a high score get a maintenance ticket, the others keep running. the planner looks at the ticket and the wind forecast, and crews only climb when the wind is below twelve metres per second, otherwise the planner reschedules the ticket for the next calm day. the crew replaces the worn part and records it in the asset system. if the turbine still vibrates after the restart the crew calls the manufacturer's engineer.

errors.detail: The 'Score high?' decision has no 'no' outcome, so the path where turbines with a low score keep running is missing.
'Reschedule Ticket' is a dead end. The text says the planner reschedules the ticket for the next calm day, so the flow should return to the ticket or planner and the wind check should be repeated.
'Wind below 12 m/s?' is fed by 'Wind Forecast', which is only a data source. The planner makes this decision, so the edge into it should come from 'Planner'.

description: a caller dials the emergency line and the call taker asks the triage questions. the triage software gives a priority, and priority one calls go straight to the nearest ambulance while lower priorities wait in the queue for a free crew. if no ambulance is free within eight minutes for a priority one call the dispatcher sends a fire engine as first responder. the crew treats the patient on scene and decides whether they need hospital. patients who don't are discharged at home, the others are taken to the emergency department, which the crew pre-alerts by radio.

errors.detail: Triage Software only connects to Priority One. Priority Two (lower priorities) has no incoming edge, so the path from the triage priority to the queue is missing, and there is no decision splitting priority one from the rest.

The 'no' outcome of 'Ambulance free in 8 minutes?' goes to Nearest Ambulance. When no ambulance is free within eight minutes, the dispatcher should send a fire engine, so it should go to Fire Engine. The 'yes' outcome has no edge.
Dispatcher has an unconditional 'sends' edge to Fire Engine, which bypasses the eight-minute condition. The fire engine should be sent only when no ambulance is free in time.
Dispatcher has no incoming edge. The priority-one ambulance wait is never routed to the dispatcher or the eight-minute check, so the check is disconnected from the flow.
Nearest Ambulance and Fire Engine dead-end. Only Free Crew leads to treating the patient, so priority-one responders never reach the on-scene treatment step.

There is no 'needs hospital?' decision box. The Patient box fans out to Hospital, Discharged and Emergency Department with unlabeled-condition edges instead of yes/no outcomes from the crew's decision, and the extra Hospital box is not a described step.

The edge Radio Pre-Alert -> Patient ('alerts') creates a loop the text does not describe. The crew pre-alerts the emergency department by radio, and the diagram also draws the pre-alert as coming from the ED rather than from the crew.

description: parents apply online and the council's admissions system checks the home address. children inside the catchment get a place offer from the school, everyone else goes on the waiting list ranked by distance. parents have two weeks to accept, and offers that aren't accepted in time are withdrawn and given to the next child on the waiting list. accepted offers go to the school office, which sends the welcome pack. parents who are refused can appeal to the independent panel, and if the panel upholds the appeal the school has to offer a place.

errors.detail: There is no catchment decision (e.g. 'Inside catchment?'). The text says children inside the catchment get an offer and everyone else goes on the waiting list, but the diagram has no yes/no split.

The edge School -> Waiting List 'routes to' is invented. The waiting list is for children outside the catchment, not something the school routes its own offers to. Council Admissions also sends every applicant to School unconditionally.
Withdrawn Offer goes to School Office. The text says a withdrawn offer is given to the next child on the waiting list, not sent to the school office.

The 'yes' outcome of 'Offer accepted?' is missing. Accepted offers should go to the School Office, which then sends the welcome pack. As drawn, the School Office is reached only through the withdrawn-offer path.
The Waiting List is a dead end. Nothing offers a place to the next child on the list when an offer is withdrawn, and the loop back to offers is absent.
The School's offer never feeds into 'Offer accepted?'. That decision hangs off Parents, so the offer-then-accept sequence is not shown.
'Refused?' is checked by Parents, but refusal is a decision by the admissions system or school. Its 'no' path is also not shown.
When the panel upholds the appeal, the 'Offer Place' box is not connected to the School, which the text says must make the offer.

description: a taxpayer files a return through the tax portal, which runs it through the validation engine. returns with errors are sent back to the taxpayer to fix, and the rest go to the risk scorer. low risk returns are paid automatically by the treasury system, anything above that waits for a case officer. the case officer asks the taxpayer for receipts and if they don't arrive within thirty days the officer rejects the refund. otherwise the officer approves it and the treasury system pays it.

errors.detail: The case officer's request for receipts goes to a 'Receipts' box instead of to the Taxpayer, so the taxpayer is never asked.
'Receipts late?' has only a 'yes' edge. The 'no' (receipts arrive in time) path to approval is missing.
Case Officer connects directly to 'Officer approves' with no condition, so approval bypasses the receipts check and happens regardless of whether receipts arrive.
After approval the flow goes to a separate 'Pays' box instead of the Treasury System, which the text says pays the refund. Treasury System has no outgoing payment step.
'Receipts late?' is checked from the 'Receipts' box rather than by the Case Officer, who makes the decision.

description: the courier scans a parcel at the locker bank and the locker controller looks for a free compartment of the right size. if there isn't one the courier takes the parcel back to the depot, otherwise the controller opens the door and the courier drops the parcel in. the controller texts the recipient a pickup code. a recipient who doesn't collect within three days gets a reminder, and after five days the controller flags the parcel for return and the courier picks it up on the next round.

errors.detail: There is no decision box such as 'Free compartment?' with yes/no outcomes. 'Right size compartment' is a plain box, so the 'no free compartment' versus 'otherwise' branching is lost.
The courier 'takes back to' the Door, but the text says the courier takes the parcel back to the depot when no compartment is free.
The courier 'drops parcel' to the Depot, but the text says the courier drops the parcel into the opened locker compartment. This is swapped with the take-back edge.
The 'Recipient miss?' decision is checked by the Recipient, but the controller handles the collection timing and decides on the reminder and the return flag.
The reminder is sent to the recipient, but the diagram routes 'Reminder' back to the Locker Controller, which the text does not describe.
The five-day flag-for-return step is not conditioned on the recipient still not having collected. The controller flags the parcel directly, and the three-day and five-day timing is missing.

description: the shot firer loads the blast holes and wires them to the firing box. before every blast the site supervisor sweeps the exclusion zone and the blast only goes ahead when the zone is clear, if anyone is inside the supervisor sounds the siren and sweeps again. the shot firer fires the blast and waits fifteen minutes for fumes. then he inspects the face for misfires, and any misfired hole is reported to the mine manager who decides whether to refire it. after the all clear the loader moves in to dig the broken rock.

errors.detail: When someone is inside, the supervisor sounds the siren and sweeps again, but the Siren/sweep path never returns to the 'Zone Clear?' check and dead-ends at Exclusion Zone.
'Zone Clear?' yes goes to Blast Holes, but a clear zone should lead to the shot firer firing the blast; there is no fire-blast step.
The sweep of the Exclusion Zone is attributed to the Siren rather than the Site Supervisor, and the supervisor has no sweep edge to the zone.
The 'Misfire?' no outcome is absent; with no misfire the process should continue to the all clear and the loader, but nothing follows.
The mine manager's decision on whether to refire is not a decision box. Mine Manager goes straight to Refire Hole, with no 'no' path for not refiring.
The Loader has no incoming edge from the all clear, and the edge to 'Dig Broken Rock' uses a box that isn't in the boxes list, so the digging step is disconnected.
The firing step is missing and the fumes wait is not sequenced before the inspection (Fumes does not lead to Face Inspection), so the ordering of fire, wait and inspect is lost.

description: the brewer mashes the grain and the wort goes to the kettle for the boil. the chiller cools the wort into the fermenter and the brewer pitches yeast. the lab takes a gravity reading every day and the beer moves to the conditioning tank only once the gravity stops dropping, until then it stays in the fermenter. from conditioning the beer is filtered and goes either to the canning line or the keg filler, depending on the order. any can that the fill checker finds underfilled is kicked off the line.

errors.detail: There is no edge from Kettle to Chiller, so the boiled wort never reaches the chiller and the flow breaks after the kettle.
The Fill Checker is attached to the Keg Filler, but the text says it checks cans, so the edge should come from the Canning Line. The Canning Line is left as a dead end.
Nothing connects the Fermenter (or the yeast pitching) to the Lab's daily gravity reading, so the gravity check and its loop are cut off from the main flow.

description: a doping control officer collects a urine sample from the athlete and splits it into an a bottle and a b bottle. both bottles go to the accredited lab. the lab tests the a sample and negative results are reported to the federation and closed. if the a sample is positive the federation notifies the athlete, who can ask for the b sample to be tested. when the b sample confirms it the federation suspends the athlete, otherwise the case is dropped.

errors.detail: The 'no' outcome of 'Sample Negative?' goes to Closed. Negative results are the ones reported to the federation and closed, and the non-negative (positive) result should go on to the positive-sample path.
After a negative result is reported, the Federation never leads to Closed. The 'yes' branch ends at Federation, which instead continues into the positive-sample check.
'Sample Positive?' is checked from Federation, but the lab's A-sample test determines it. This also makes negative reports flow into the positive check.

'B Sample positive?' is checked from Federation, not from the B-bottle test at the lab. It is reached regardless of whether the athlete asked for the B test. The 'Bottle Test' box dead-ends and is not connected to the B bottle, the lab or this decision.
The Federation notifying the athlete is not drawn. The 'yes' edge goes from the decision straight to Athlete, with no Federation 'notifies' edge.

description: a client sends a document to the translation agency's project manager, who gets a quote from the pricing tool. if the client accepts the quote the project manager assigns a translator, else the request is archived. the translator works in the cat tool, which checks every segment against the translation memory and fills in exact matches automatically. a proofreader checks the finished translation and sends anything with errors back to the translator. the project manager delivers the final file and the billing team invoices the client.

errors.detail: No edge sends the translation from the Translator or Cat Tool to the Proofreader, so the Proofreader has no incoming flow.
The 'no' outcome of 'Errors found?' is missing; the error-free translation should go to the Project Manager for delivery.
The Project Manager's 'delivers file' edge goes to the Billing Team, but the final file is delivered to the Client. The Client delivery edge is missing.

The 'Translation Agency' box sits between Client and Project Manager. The text says the client sends the document to the project manager, and 'gets quote from' is the wrong relation for the Translation Agency to Project Manager edge.
The edge to 'Exact Matches' uses a box that is not in the box list, and the text describes no such step.

description: each elevator reports faults to the remote monitoring service. the service tries to reset the elevator remotely, and if the reset works it logs the fault and does nothing else. when the reset fails it raises a call with the maintenance dispatcher, who sends the nearest technician. if someone is trapped inside the dispatcher also calls the fire brigade. the technician repairs the elevator and the monitoring service watches it for an hour before closing the call.

errors.detail: Reset worked? has no 'no' edge, and the separate 'Reset failed?' box has no incoming edge, so a failed reset never leads to the Maintenance Dispatcher.

The duplicate 'Technician' and 'Monitoring Service' boxes, plus the 'shows repair' edge, are invented. The technician should repair the Elevator, and the original Remote Monitoring Service should then watch it. As drawn, the repair/watch/close part is disconnected from the main flow.
'Call Closed' hangs off Monitoring Service in parallel with the one-hour watch, rather than following it. The text says the call is closed only after the hour of watching.

description: a skier books skis online and the rental system reserves a pair in their size at the shop. at the shop the technician adjusts the bindings to the skier's weight and the skier signs the waiver. skis come back at the end of the day through the return counter, where staff check them for damage. damaged skis go to the repair bench, the rest are waxed and put back on the rack. if the repair bench can't fix them the shop manager writes them off.

errors.detail: There is no 'Damaged?' decision after the staff inspection. 'Damage' is an ordinary box with unlabeled edges to both Repair Bench and Wax, so every ski goes to both paths instead of damaged skis going to repair (yes) and the rest being waxed and racked (no).

description: farmers send seed samples to the seed bank, where a technician cleans and counts them. the technician runs a germination test, and samples that germinate below eighty five percent are sent back to the farmer for a fresh sample. good samples are dried to five percent moisture and sealed in foil bags. the bags go to the minus twenty vault. every ten years the curator retests a portion of each sample, and if germination has dropped the curator asks the regeneration field to grow fresh seed.

errors.detail: Good samples (germination at or above 85%) should go from the decision box's 'no' outcome to drying, but the diagram has no 'no' edge and instead routes the sent-back Fresh Sample into Dried Sample, so the good-sample path is missing and replaced by an invalid one.

description: sewage arrives at the treatment works and passes through the screens, which remove rags into a skip. the grit channel settles out sand and the flow goes on to the primary tanks. the aeration lanes treat the water next, and there are four lanes using round robin. a turbidity sensor sits in front of the river outfall and diverts any cloudy water back to the aeration lanes. sludge from the primary tanks is pumped to the digester, which makes biogas for the generator.

errors.detail: No edge leads from Screens to Grit Channel, so the grit channel is disconnected from the flow and the main path breaks after the screens.
Aeration Lanes has no edge to the Turbidity Sensor. The sensor sits in front of the River Outfall, so treated water should go from the lanes to the sensor and then to the outfall.
The send-back edge runs from River Outfall to Aeration Lanes, but the text says the turbidity sensor diverts cloudy water back to the lanes. The cloudy water never reaches the outfall.
The cloudy-water condition has no decision box such as 'Water cloudy?', with yes leading back to the Aeration Lanes and no leading to the River Outfall. The clear-water outcome is not drawn.

description: a steward finds a lost item and hands it to the lost and found desk. the desk logs it in the property system and anything valuable goes into the safe. when a fan reports a lost item online the property system searches for a match. on a match the desk emails the fan to collect it, and on a miss the system keeps the report open for thirty days. unclaimed items are given to charity after ninety days, except phones, which the desk wipes and recycles.

errors.detail: The steward hands the item to a separate 'Lost and Found' box, not to the 'Desk' that logs it, so the Desk has no incoming edge and the item flow is split.
The fan's online report of a lost item to the property system is missing. The diagram instead has Property System pointing to Fan with 'searches for match'.
The 'Match found?' decision is checked by Fan, but the property system performs the search and makes that decision.
The yes outcome of 'Match found?' loops back to Property System, but on a match the desk emails the fan to collect the item. That email step is missing.
The miss path is missing from the real match decision. The property system should keep the report open on a miss.
A duplicate 'Match?' decision checked by Desk sends 'yes' to 'Keep report open', but keeping the report open happens on a miss, checked by the property system.
'Unclaimed items' goes straight to Charity and bypasses the 'Phone?' decision, so phones are not excluded from the charity path.
The 'no' outcome of 'Phone?' to Charity is missing, and the Desk checks 'Phone?' directly instead of it applying to unclaimed items.
'Unclaimed items' has no incoming link from stored items or open reports, and the ninety-day and thirty-day limits are not shown.

description: a family fills in an adoption form at the shelter and the adoption counsellor reviews it. families with a garden and no other dogs move straight to a meet and greet, the rest get a home visit first. if the home visit fails the counsellor declines the application. at the meet and greet the behaviourist watches the dog with the family, and only if the behaviourist is happy does the family pay the fee. the vet microchips the dog before it goes home.

errors.detail: The 'Home visit failed?' decision has no 'no' edge. A family that passes the home visit should go on to the meet and greet, but that path is missing.
The 'Dog-free garden?' decision is fed by Family. The adoption counsellor reviews the form and sorts families, so the edge should come from the counsellor. As drawn, the counsellor box dead-ends.
The 'yes' outcome of 'Home visit failed?' goes to a generic 'Application' box. The text says the counsellor declines the application, so it should lead to a declined outcome tied to the counsellor.
The vet microchips the dog before it goes home, but the diagram has no step for the dog going home. It also labels the Pay Fee to Vet edge 'goes to' rather than showing microchipping.

description: an advertiser books a radio spot through the sales rep, who checks the traffic system for free slots. if the slot is taken the rep offers the next free slot, and the advertiser either takes it or cancels. the creative team records the ad and legal reviews the script. ads that make health claims need sign off from the compliance manager. the traffic system then schedules the ad into the playout system, which plays it and sends a proof of play to billing.

errors.detail: The 'no' outcome of 'Slot taken?' is missing. When the slot is free the booking should simply go ahead, but no edge shows this.
'Take Slot' loops back to Advertiser instead of moving the booking forward (creative recording and review, then scheduling). The accepted-slot path dead-ends.
Nothing connects the booking to the Creative Team recording the ad. Creative Team has no incoming edge, and the 'records the ad' step is not shown.
There is no decision box such as 'Health claims?' with yes and no outcomes. The compliance sign-off is not conditional, and the path for ads without health claims is missing.
The edge 'Advertiser -> Compliance Manager (needs sign off)' is invented. The ad that makes health claims needs sign-off, not the advertiser, and it comes after the legal review.
Legal and Compliance Manager lead nowhere. The approved ad is never linked to the Traffic System scheduling it into Playout, so the review chain is cut off from the rest of the process.

description: the archivist pulls a box of letters and the conservator checks each letter's condition. fragile letters go to the conservation studio to be repaired first, the others go straight to the scanning room. the scanner operator scans each letter and the ocr service extracts the text. pages where the ocr confidence is low go to volunteers to transcribe by hand. the catalogue publishes the scans with the text and the archivist returns the box to the stacks.

errors.detail: The 'Fragile letters?' decision is fed by OCR Service (with a 'yes' label) instead of by the Conservator, who checks each letter's condition.
The edge Conservator -> Conservation Studio ('routes to') sends every letter to the studio. The text sends only fragile letters there, and only through the decision.
There is no edge from Conservation Studio to Scanning Room, though repaired letters go on to scanning after repair.
Scanning Room has no outgoing edge to Scanner Operator, so the flow dead-ends there and the Scanner Operator is never reached.
The 'no' path from 'OCR low confidence?' is missing. Pages with good confidence should go on to the Catalogue.
Hand Transcription dead-ends. The transcribed text should go to the Catalogue for publishing.
The 'publishes scans' edge goes from Catalogue to Archivist. Publishing has no recipient in the text, and the Archivist's return of the box is a separate step.

description: green beans arrive from the importer and the quality lab roasts a small sample. if the sample cups below eighty points the roastery returns the lot to the importer. accepted lots go to the warehouse until the head roaster schedules them. the roaster drops each batch into the cooling tray and the colour meter reads it, and batches outside the target colour are sold as seconds. good batches rest for two days, then the packing machine bags them and the web shop ships orders.

errors.detail: The 'no' outcome of 'Sample under 80 points?' is missing, so accepted lots never come from the decision. Instead the Roastery, which also receives the rejected 'yes' path, sends lots to the Warehouse.
The Cooling Tray is fed from the Roastery, not from the roaster who schedules lots out of the Warehouse. The Warehouse→Head Roaster path dead-ends, and rejected lots appear to continue into roasting.

A redundant 'Good Batch?' decision is added and fed straight from the Colour Meter. The text has no such second check, and the 'yes' outcome of 'Target Colour?' should lead on to resting and packing. That edge is missing and 'Good Batch?' has no 'no' branch.
The two-day rest of good batches before packing is not represented.

description: a drone flies along the bridge and photographs every girder. the photos go to a crack detection model, which flags any crack longer than five millimetres. the bridge engineer reviews the flagged photos and sends a rope access team for anything she can't judge from the photo. if the team or the engineer finds a serious crack the engineer closes a lane and orders a repair, otherwise the crack is added to the watch list. the drone rechecks watch list cracks every three months.

errors.detail: The engineer's choice to send the rope access team only for photos she can't judge has no decision box, so the diagram has her send the team for every flagged crack.
The Rope Access Team box has no outgoing edge, so the team's findings never reach the 'Serious crack?' decision and the flow dead-ends there.
The photos are sent from the Girder box to the model, but the drone takes the photos and the text has them go from the drone.
The drone's recheck of watch list cracks has no every-three-months timing, and the diagram does not show the recheck feeding back into photographing and detection.

description: the launch director polls each console for a go. propulsion, range safety and weather all report to the director. if any console says no go the director holds the count, fixes the issue and polls again. on a full go the ground computer runs the terminal count. the flight computer takes over at ten seconds and aborts the launch on any sensor fault, otherwise it ignites the engines and releases the clamps.

errors.detail: After fixing the issue, 'Poll Again' leads on to the Ground Computer instead of looping back to the Launch Director or Console to poll again.
The 'Console no?' decision has no 'no' (full go) outcome leading to the Ground Computer running the terminal count. The Ground Computer is reached only through the hold/fix/poll path.
No edge connects Terminal Count to the Flight Computer taking over at ten seconds, so the flow dead-ends and the Flight Computer branch is disconnected.

description: teams submit their projects on the hackathon site, which checks the submission has a demo video. submissions without a video are marked incomplete and the site emails the team, who can resubmit until the deadline. complete submissions are split across judges using round robin. each judge scores the project and projects with a big score gap between judges go to the head judge to break the tie. the organisers announce the top three from the final scores.

errors.detail: The 'yes' outcome of 'Demo video?' goes back to Teams (and is duplicated) instead of passing the complete submission on to the judges' round-robin split.
'Demo video?' has no 'no' edge to 'Submissions incomplete'. Instead 'Teams' is wired straight to 'Submissions incomplete', so the check does not drive the incomplete path.
'Submissions incomplete' feeds into 'Judges (round robin)', but only complete submissions are split across judges.
The resubmit loop goes from 'Team' straight to 'Demo video?' rather than back to the hackathon site's submission step. The deadline limit is also missing, and 'Team' duplicates 'Teams'.
There is no decision box for a big score gap between judges. Judges send everything to the Head Judge, and the path where there is no big gap, going straight to final scores, is missing.
'Head Judge' points to 'Organisers' rather than producing the final scores. The tie-break result should feed 'Final scores', which the organisers then announce from.
The edge 'Organisers' to 'Final scores' ('announce from') is drawn in the opposite direction, since the top three are announced from the scores.

description: the manufacturer ships vaccine boxes with a temperature logger to the national store. the store manager reads the logger on arrival and quarantines any box that went above eight degrees, the rest go into the walk in fridge. district nurses order vaccines from the store every week and the store packs them in cool boxes with ice packs. at the clinic the nurse checks the vial monitor and only uses vials whose monitor hasn't changed colour. used vials are counted and the count goes back to the store manager for restocking.

errors.detail: The 'Monitor changed?' decision is fed by the Vial Monitor box, but the text says the nurse checks the monitor and decides which vials to use.
The Cool Box goes to the Vial Monitor, but the text has the store sending the cool boxes to the district nurse at the clinic. The nurse has no link to the clinic steps.
The 'yes' outcome of 'Monitor changed?', where vials with a changed monitor are not used, has no edge.

The manufacturer ships to the Temperature Logger, which then 'routes to' the store. The text says the manufacturer ships vaccine boxes, with a logger, to the national store. The vaccine boxes are not modelled and the logger is wrongly placed as an intermediate step.
The count going back to the store manager 'for restocking' has no restocking step.
